review.result: Re-inspected the mapped CLI, authenticated server, session, SDK, permission, and custom-tool source at v1.18.25 commit cb7d8b2f5e44876ef98b661dc10590c915af3a9f and the complete downstream diff through 6883ca5bd35a5494fb2759018373308911c79e01 for generation-attempt tool leases. Confirmed provider sessions are explicitly created/resumed and tool context identifies provider sessions; inline tool configuration and permissions remain server supplied. The application-owned generation/attempt lifetime is a local authorization boundary, not an upstream session guarantee. Missing-session retries receive new opaque leases; prior attempts, cancellation, and completion cannot retain authority. No runtime version, transport, provider schema, or permission expansion is introduced. Re-inspected the custom-tool definition, plugin package, and configuration loader at the same upstream commit for live diagnostics recovery. tool.schema is Zod and the definition retains descriptions; explicit configuration directories are supported. Added model-facing cursor provenance guidance and a bounded invalid-cursor recovery message without changing server authorization. Live evidence showed an invented initial cursor, not a stale lease. Inspected the custom-tool registry, provider schema transformations, and LLM tool handoff at that same commit: the registry converts Zod input schemas, and optional-field nullability transformations are provider-specific. Repeated OpenRouter GPT calls supplied every optional selector despite omission guidance. The adapter now explicitly admits null for unused optional selectors and removes nulls before the server request; invented non-null cursors remain rejected. This is an adapter input-schema extension, not a server query or permission expansion. Final review verified that null-only identity/correlation objects must be omitted after normalization because the server rejects empty selectors. Added adapter-to-broker regression coverage while retaining non-empty selector values and the existing upstream schema contract. PR review follow-up preserves attempt correlation in structured retry logging and reads command audit identity directly from the lease rather than an independently evicted cache. No upstream invocation or schema behavior changes; the same exact source audit applies. Re-inspected the recorded upstream CLI/server, session, SDK, permission and custom-tool sources and complete admitted downstream diff for protected-work return scheduling. Confirmed explicit prompt/session selection, abort signals and server-supplied permissions remain unchanged. Protected exclusion, durable return/relevance validation and idempotent delivery are application-owned. Catch-up invokes the existing read-only runner with history access and no room-command tools or writer grant; no OpenCode schema, transport or supported version changes. Confirmed model-list output remains provider/model lines and MCP configuration remains unchanged at the recorded source commits; all five mapped contract suites pass. PR pre-merge review rechecked every recorded upstream path at the same exact commit and the complete admitted downstream diff. Protected admission now reports a non-cancelling blocked turn so ordinary staged conversation can try other participants. This is local scheduling behavior; OpenCode invocation, cancellation, session, permissions, and model/MCP configuration contracts are unchanged. Return no-update cursor revalidation and superseded-text rejection are enforced by the application. Re-inspected all structured-sdk-server paths at upstream v1.18.25 commit cb7d8b2f5e44876ef98b661dc10590c915af3a9f and the complete downstream diff through 6883ca5bd35a5494fb2759018373308911c79e01. Confirmed explicit listener/auth configuration, directory-aware SDK requests, typed health responses, session output format and downstream structured-output retry validation. Repository readiness adds an application route and does not change OpenCode startup, authentication, transport, prompts, or runtime compatibility. Runtime identity remains pinned; no new upstream behavior is inferred.

surfaces.description: Authenticated loopback server startup, exact runtime health negotiation, typed session prompts, cancellation, and locally validated structured room turns.
OpenCode run arguments, JSONL events, sessions, variants, errors, and provider telemetry.
Runtime version bounds and the human-formatted models --verbose compatibility parser.
Inline OpenCode permissions, the custom-tool API, and the server-owned tool configuration directory.
The mergeable OpenCode MCP configuration and consultation-skill adapter.
